parts.title: Orientation
parts.summary: What Latin is, the one idea that runs through its grammar, and how this guide works.

parts.title: Sounds and script
parts.summary: The restored classical pronunciation, vowel length, syllable weight and stress, and how Latin has been spelled.

parts.title: The simplest sentences
parts.summary: A verb alone, a doer, a thing acted on, being, negation, yes/no questions and agreement.

parts.title: Nouns and their machinery
parts.summary: The six cases, the five declensions, pronouns and pointing words.

parts.title: Verbs: the core system
parts.summary: Stems, tenses, the passive, deponents, the irregular verbs and the subjunctive.

parts.title: Modifying and linking
parts.summary: Adjectives, adverbs, comparison, numbers, connectives, participles and the finer uses of the cases.

parts.title: Complex sentences
parts.summary: Questions, relative clauses, the ablative absolute, reported speech and the subordinate subjunctive.

parts.title: Advanced and special topics
parts.summary: Gerund and gerundive, impersonals, style, metre, word formation, and Latin before and after the classical norm.

parts.title: Reading real texts
parts.summary: Eight graded passages from graffiti to Vergil and a medieval charter, walked through line by line.

parts.title: Reference
parts.summary: Paradigm tables, glossary of terms and abbreviations, annotated bibliography.

lessons.title: What Latin is
lessons.point: Place Latin in time, space and family, and know which Latin this guide teaches

lessons.title: The organising idea: endings carry the grammar
lessons.point: See how one word changes its ending to do the jobs English gives to word order and helper words

lessons.title: How to use this guide and where its facts come from
lessons.point: Read the examples, glosses, confidence labels and source notes used throughout

lessons.title: The alphabet and the vowels, short and long
lessons.point: Pronounce the five vowels in both lengths and see why length matters

lessons.title: Diphthongs and consonants
lessons.point: Pronounce every Latin letter as an educated Roman of Cicero's day did

lessons.title: Syllables: light and heavy
lessons.point: Divide any word into syllables and tell which are heavy

lessons.title: Stress: the second-from-last rule
lessons.point: Stress any Latin word correctly from its spelling alone

lessons.title: Spelling in the wild: capitals, u and v, i and j
lessons.point: Read Latin as printed in different editions, inscriptions and manuscripts

lessons.title: A verb is a sentence
lessons.point: Say who does something with a single word, using the six person endings

lessons.title: Naming the doer: the nominative
lessons.point: Add a named doer to a verb and make the two agree in number

lessons.title: The thing acted on: the accusative
lessons.point: Mark the object of a verb and read a sentence whatever order its words come in

lessons.title: Three genders
lessons.point: Sort nouns into masculine, feminine and neuter and predict their nominative and accusative

lessons.title: Being: sum, es, est
lessons.point: Say that something is something, and that something exists

lessons.title: Saying no and asking yes or no
lessons.point: Negate a sentence with nōn and turn it into a question with -ne, nōnne or num

lessons.title: Describing: adjectives agree
lessons.point: Attach an adjective to a noun by matching gender, number and case

lessons.title: Word order and emphasis
lessons.point: Choose a word order for a reason, and read what an author's order is telling you

lessons.title: The case system: six jobs, five patterns
lessons.point: Read a dictionary entry, find a noun's stem and know what each case is for

lessons.title: The genitive: one noun hanging on another
lessons.point: Say whose something is, and what it is a part or kind of

lessons.title: The dative: the person concerned
lessons.point: Mark the receiver or the person affected, and say that someone has something

lessons.title: The ablative: from, with, in
lessons.point: Mark source, tool and setting, alone and with prepositions

lessons.title: Prepositions and the cases they take
lessons.point: Use the common prepositions and choose between accusative and ablative after in and sub

lessons.title: Calling someone, and the first two declensions complete
lessons.point: Address a person, handle nouns like puer and ager, and hold the full first and second declensions

lessons.title: The third declension: consonant stems
lessons.point: Decline nouns like rēx and nōmen and explain why their nominative looks different from the rest

lessons.title: The third declension: i-stems
lessons.point: Recognise i-stem nouns and their four distinctive endings

lessons.title: The fourth and fifth declensions
lessons.point: Decline nouns like manus and rēs

lessons.title: I, you, we and self
lessons.point: Use ego, tū, nōs, vōs and the reflexive sē, with their possessive adjectives

lessons.title: is, ea, id: he, she, it and that
lessons.point: Refer back to someone or something already mentioned

lessons.title: Pointing: hic, ille, iste, ipse, īdem
lessons.point: Point at things near, far and aforementioned, and say self and same

lessons.title: Place and time without prepositions
lessons.point: Say where, where to, where from, when and for how long, including the locative

lessons.title: How a verb is built: stems and principal parts
lessons.point: Read a verb's dictionary entry and know which stem builds which forms

lessons.title: The present of the third and fourth conjugations
lessons.point: Conjugate verbs like regō, capiō and audiō and explain their short linking vowel

lessons.title: The infinitive, with can, want and must
lessons.point: Name an action and attach it to possum, volō, nōlō, mālō and dēbeō

lessons.title: The imperfect: a past in progress
lessons.point: Describe what was going on or used to happen

lessons.title: The future: two ways to make it
lessons.point: Form the future in all four conjugations and see why there are two patterns

lessons.title: The perfect: a completed act
lessons.point: Form the perfect from the third principal part with its own set of endings

lessons.title: Choosing a past tense
lessons.point: Decide between perfect and imperfect, and read the two senses of the perfect

lessons.title: Before then: pluperfect and future perfect
lessons.point: Place one event before another in the past or the future

lessons.title: Commands
lessons.point: Tell someone to do something, and not to do it

lessons.title: The passive: the -r endings
lessons.point: Turn a sentence round so that the thing acted on becomes the subject

lessons.title: The perfect participle and the perfect passive
lessons.point: Build amātus est and its relatives from the fourth principal part

lessons.title: Deponent verbs: passive in form, active in meaning
lessons.point: Recognise and use verbs like sequor, loquor and morior

lessons.title: Irregular verbs: eō and ferō
lessons.point: Conjugate go and carry and their many compounds

lessons.title: Irregular verbs: fīō, dō and the rest
lessons.point: Use fīō as the passive of faciō, and handle dō, edō and defective verbs like inquit and meminī

lessons.title: Compound verbs and what prefixes do to them
lessons.point: Take a compound apart, and explain why faciō becomes cōnficiō

lessons.title: The subjunctive: present and imperfect forms
lessons.point: Form the mood Latin uses for what is wished, intended or imagined

lessons.title: The subjunctive: perfect and pluperfect forms
lessons.point: Complete the subjunctive in the active and passive

lessons.title: The subjunctive on its own
lessons.point: Express a wish, a proposal, a doubt or a possibility in a main clause

lessons.title: Third-declension adjectives
lessons.point: Make adjectives like omnis, ācer and fēlīx agree with any noun

lessons.title: Adjectives as nouns, and the ūnus group
lessons.point: Read bonī as good men and decline ūnus, sōlus, tōtus, alius and their kin

lessons.title: Adverbs
lessons.point: Turn an adjective into an adverb and learn the common adverbs that are not derived

lessons.title: More and most: comparison
lessons.point: Form comparatives and superlatives and say than in two ways

lessons.title: Numbers
lessons.point: Count, decline ūnus, duo, trēs and mīlle, and form ordinals

lessons.title: Linking words
lessons.point: Join words and sentences with et, -que, atque, aut, vel, sed, nam, enim, autem, igitur and tamen

lessons.title: Participles: present and future
lessons.point: Form amāns and amātūrus and use participles where English uses a clause

lessons.title: The ablative sorted out
lessons.point: Tell apart the ablatives of means, manner, cause, separation, respect, description and comparison

lessons.title: The genitive and dative sorted out
lessons.point: Read partitive and objective genitives, datives of purpose and verbs that take the dative

lessons.title: Someone, anyone, each, no one
lessons.point: Use aliquis, quis, quisquam, quisque, quīdam, nēmō and nihil

lessons.title: Questions with question words
lessons.point: Ask who, what, which, where, when, why and how

lessons.title: Relative clauses: quī, quae, quod
lessons.point: Attach a clause to a noun, taking gender and number from the noun and case from the clause

lessons.title: When and because: clauses with the indicative
lessons.point: Use ubi, postquam, dum, antequam, quod and quia

lessons.title: The ablative absolute
lessons.point: Compress a background clause into a noun and participle in the ablative

lessons.title: Reported statements: the accusative and infinitive
lessons.point: Report what someone says, thinks or sees, with all six infinitives

lessons.title: Sequence of tenses
lessons.point: Choose the tense of a subordinate subjunctive from the tense of the main verb

lessons.title: Purpose: ut and nē
lessons.point: Say what something is done in order to achieve

lessons.title: Result: so … that
lessons.point: Say what followed as a consequence, and tell result from purpose

lessons.title: Indirect commands and fears
lessons.point: Report an order or request, and express what someone is afraid may happen

lessons.title: Indirect questions
lessons.point: Embed a question under a verb of asking, knowing or telling

lessons.title: cum: when, since, although
lessons.point: Read the commonest subordinating word in Latin prose in all its senses

lessons.title: Conditions: if
lessons.point: Build open, future and unreal conditions and know what each mood claims

lessons.title: Although, provided that, as if
lessons.point: Use quamquam, quamvīs, etsī, dummodo and quasi

lessons.title: Relative clauses with the subjunctive; quīn and quōminus
lessons.point: Read the sort of person who, and clauses after verbs of doubting and preventing

lessons.title: The gerund: the verb as a noun
lessons.point: Use the verbal noun in -ndum in the cases the infinitive cannot supply

lessons.title: The gerundive: what must be done
lessons.point: Express obligation with the gerundive and the dative of the agent, and read gerundive phrases

lessons.title: The supine
lessons.point: Read the two fossil verbal nouns in -um and -ū

lessons.title: Impersonal verbs and the impersonal passive
lessons.point: Use licet, oportet, pudet and read pugnātur as there is fighting

lessons.title: Extended reported speech
lessons.point: Follow a whole speech reported in ōrātiō oblīqua, with its clauses, commands and questions

lessons.title: Word order as style
lessons.point: Read separated phrases, framed clauses and the periodic sentence

lessons.title: Poetry I: quantity, elision and the hexameter
lessons.point: Scan a line of Vergil

lessons.title: Poetry II: the elegiac couplet and poetic grammar
lessons.point: Scan a couplet and recognise the forms and constructions poets prefer

lessons.title: Word formation
lessons.point: Work out an unknown word from its root and suffix

lessons.title: Names, dates and Roman numerals
lessons.point: Read a Roman name, a Roman date and a number written in numerals

lessons.title: Early and colloquial Latin
lessons.point: Recognise the archaic forms of Plautus and old inscriptions, and the signs of everyday speech

lessons.title: After the classics: late, church and medieval Latin
lessons.point: Adjust your classical Latin to read the Vulgate and medieval documents

lessons.title: Inscriptions and manuscripts
lessons.point: Expand the common abbreviations of stone and parchment and read an edited text's signs

lessons.title: Reading 1: voices from the walls of Pompeii
lessons.point: Read real graffiti and short inscriptions

lessons.title: Reading 2: the Vulgate, Genesis 1.1–5
lessons.point: Read a plain late-Latin narrative

lessons.title: Reading 3: Caesar, Gallic War 1.1
lessons.point: Read the opening of the most famous piece of plain classical prose

lessons.title: Reading 4: Catullus 85 and 5
lessons.point: Read two short poems and scan them

lessons.title: Reading 5: Phaedrus, The Wolf and the Lamb
lessons.point: Read a verse fable

lessons.title: Reading 6: Cicero, Against Catiline 1.1–2
lessons.point: Read oratory at full pressure

lessons.title: Reading 7: Vergil, Aeneid 1.1–11
lessons.point: Read the opening of the Aeneid

lessons.title: Reading 8: Magna Carta, clauses 39 and 40
lessons.point: Read medieval legal Latin from a document

lessons.title: Tables: nouns, adjectives and pronouns
lessons.point: Look up any nominal ending

lessons.title: Tables: verbs
lessons.point: Look up any verb form

lessons.title: Glossary of terms and abbreviations
lessons.point: Look up any technical term or gloss abbreviation used in the guide

lessons.title: Annotated bibliography
lessons.point: Know what each source is and where to go next
